title: Microsoft Purview: per-policy coverage report for auto-labeling (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, report navigation, progress command and documented report limits are supported. Minor corrections should cite the separate worldwide roadmap item and acknowledge the additional AIP licensing qualification in Microsoft's service description.

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-09-23T22:59:12.
Microsoft plans a per-policy report relating enforcement processing to the latest simulation.
claims.quote: For each enforced auto-labeling policy, admins can view how files processed during enforcement correlate to the latest simulation run.

claims.claim: The planned report shows volumes of labeled and not-yet-labeled files.
claims.quote: The per-policy coverage report shows volumes of files that have been labeled or are not yet labeled

claims.claim: The planned report identifies whether files were included in the latest simulation snapshot.
claims.quote: and whether those files were included in the last simulation snapshot.

claims.claim: The planned report identifies files processed during enforcement but absent from the simulation snapshot.
claims.quote: while also identifying files that were not found in the simulation snapshot but were processed during enforcement.

claims.claim: The roadmap description names no required administrator action.
claims.quote: For each enforced auto-labeling policy, admins can view how files processed during enforcement correlate to the latest simulation run.

claims.claim: Coverage is reached in the Microsoft Purview portal through Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Coverage > View coverage.
claims.quote:
go to Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. Select a policy
In the Coverage column, select View coverage.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no PowerShell or API operation for coverage-by-simulation data as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: 'auto-labeling coverage PowerShell Graph', 'auto-labeling View coverage API'. Opened apply-sensitivity-label-automatically and Get-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy; searches returned portal coverage and policy commands, not a coverage-data operation.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Per-policy review is reached through Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > View details in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: To open the newer review pages, go to Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. Select a policy, then select View details in the policy details panel.

claims.claim: Get-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -IncludeProgressFeedback retrieves the selected policy's labeling progress.
claims.quote:
The Identity parameter specifies the auto-labeling policy that you want to view.
IncludeProgressFeedback specifies whether to include the labeling progress of files in SharePoint or OneDrive.

claims.claim: The progress cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: IncludeProgressFeedback reports progress for enabled SharePoint and OneDrive policies rather than a comparison with simulation.
claims.quote: If you use this switch, the command shows the progress of files to be labeled, files labeled in the last 7 days, and total files labeled for enabled auto-labeling policies.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the government-cloud report's arrival default or whether an administrator must enable the report.
claims.quote: Searched: 'auto-labeling coverage report automatically', 'View coverage enable Purview'. Read roadmap and coverage section: policy prerequisites, not report rollout default. Purview service description's general tenant enablement does not specify this government-cloud preview report's arrival.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Included is the licensing model for a report view inside the already licensed service-side auto-labeling surface.
claims.quote: Service-side auto-labeling (SharePoint, OneDrive, Exchange) | Microsoft Purview portal → Information Protection → Policies → Auto-labeling policies | Same E5 / P2-tier SKUs as above

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The cited auto-labeling page includes service-side auto-labeling with Microsoft 365 E5, E5 Compliance, E5 Information Protection & Governance and Azure Information Protection Premium P2 (standalone).
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5, Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance, Microsoft 365 E5 Information Protection & Governance, Azure Information Protection Premium P2 (standalone)
claims.fix: Keep the attributed list, but add: 'The Microsoft Purview service description additionally says that AIP P1 must be assigned alongside AIP P2 for sensitivity labeling to be available.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-365-service-descriptions/microsoft-365-tenantlevel-services-licensing-guidance/microsoft-purview-service-description#microsoft-purview-information-protection-sensitivity-labeling and add that page to sources.

claims.claim: The cited page says auto-labeling files and emails is not included at E3 or Business Premium level.
claims.quote: You have E3 or Business Premium. Auto-labeling of files and emails isn't included at this SKU. Sensitivity labels and manual labeling are — auto-labeling requires an E5 / P2-tier add-on.

claims.claim: The policy must be turned on before coverage is reviewed.
